Mr. Speaker, last December the Right Hon. Prime Minister of Canada made it clear that constitutional talks with Quebec were not a high priority for his Government. This morning, the newspaper Le Devoir reported that apparently the Prime Minister was now prepared to start constitutional talks with Quebec and to accelerate the process. My question to the Prime Minister is as follows: Since at its convention last weekend, the Parti Quebecois decided that the issue of sovereignty or independence would not be part of its election program in the next provincial election, and since, according to Premier Levesque, an election would be held in a matter of months, is it true that the Prime Minister of Canada is prepared to resume constitutional talks with Quebec with a view to reaching an agreement with the Quebec Government before the next election?

I have a supplementary question, Mr. Speaker. The question which I have just directed to the Prime Minister is in no way a hypothetical question. It has to do with a specific motion that has been passed unanimously by the Assemblee nationale. I should like to ask the Prime Minister under what terms ... I suggest that it is a thoroughly valid condition which could serve as an interesting basis for discussion. It seems to me that if the Prime Minister would indicate to the House and to the Canadian people under what terms his government is planning to negotiate-because for negotiations to happen both sides have to forward proposals-if he could give us some indication on such a simple matter, that could facilitate the forthcoming debate.

Mr. Speaker, my question is directed to the Minister of State for Forestry. I am sure most Members know that forestry is the largest industry in Canada. A full 50 per cent of the timber harvested comes from British Columbia. In light of that, will the Minister explain why he and his Cabinet colleagues are only prepared to put forward $30 million per year for the five year Canada-B.C. reforestation agreement, when the University of British Columbia has identified a need for $600 million a year, and his own officials have identified a need for $200 million a year? Why so little money for B.C.?
